newsitem.title: USA: Sunglass stocks fall as market gets cloudy.
newsitem.headline: Sunglass stocks fall as market gets cloudy.

text.p: It's looking a little cloudier for for sunglass makers.
Stocks of sunglass makers and retailers fell Thursday as news of bloated inventories, sluggish sales and a lack of dynamic new products darkened the outlook for the industry.

The stock of sunglass manufacturer Oakley Inc. slid $3.875 to $11.50 as its largest customer, Sunglass Hut International Inc., Thursday reported November same-store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, fell 9.9 percent.

Oakley forecast fourth-quarter earnings to be below Wall Street estimates and said it saw further delays in orders from 2,022-store chain Sunglass Hut, which previously requested a delay in November orders.
Oakley's earnings rose to $15.7 million in the third quarter ended Sept. 30 from $10.2 million in the year-ago period. Sales swelled to $67.8 million from $47.5 million.

Sunglass Hut stock fell 87.5 cents to $7.375. Sunglass maker Gargoyles Inc., which went public in September at $16 a share, fell $1 to $8.625. Bausch & Lomb Inc., owner of Ray Ban, however, rose 62.5 cents to $37.

"We've been expecting a weak fourth quarter due to inventory overages at Sunglass Hut," said Eli Kammerman at Salomon Brothers. "People have reached a limit as to how many sunglasses they can wear," he said.
U.S. sales of premium priced sunglasses, which sell at more than $30 a pair, have declined about 3 percent to 4 percent in the past six months, he noted.
Analysts expect the market to remain sluggish into 1997.

"Sales trends remain soft and there will probably be some downward pressure on earnings estimates for both retailers and vendors that is likely to continue into the first half of next year," said David Buchsbaum, analyst with Southeast Research.
He said pared-down inventories and some new products should begin to help the market in the second half of 1997.

Analysts said Sunglass Hut has indicated it will try to get inventories down to about $145 million at the end of the year. In addition to 2,022 sunglass speciality locations, it operates 28 EyeX optical stores and 41 Watch Station stores.

"Basically, Sunglass Hut has tried to pare down inventories and change its product mix to include more fashion lines," said Buchsbaum. "The main factor behind the weaker sales trends is the sport category, of which Oakley is the primary vendor."

Sunglass Hut reported Thursday that sales for the four weeks ended Nov. 30 rose 11.8 percent to $28.1 million from $25.2 million in the year-ago period. But same-store sales for the four-week fiscal period fell 9.9 percent.
